subject: ML platform procurement: decision criteria, PO vs card, and security gating
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@asteria.health>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@asteria.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from Friday's intro — procurement & security checklist

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Summary of what I heard
- Asteria is evaluating a managed inference platform for in-product ML features (conversational and batch embeddings).
- Procurement prefers predictable unit economics and wants to understand payment routing (PO vs card) and marketplace options (AWS/GCP Marketplace).
- Security/compliance gating: procurement needs SOC 2 Type II evidence and an executed DPA before final approval; your vendor questionnaire also needs answers for a few control areas.

Proposed immediate actions (owners in parentheses)
1) I will share SOC 2 report + DPA template and flag any standard exceptions (Marcus).
2) Marissa will prepare a short commercial summary showing PO terms, card payment, and marketplace billing pros/cons (Marissa).
3) Ben to review the Asteria vendor questionnaire and provide concise answers for the security controls they highlighted (Ben).
4) Claire / Procurement: confirm which commercial path you prefer for an initial pilot (PO with net-30 / card / marketplace).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template.pdf

Do these actions look right? If yes, can procurement confirm the preferred payment route and a target internal sign-off date?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0126

---

From: Claire Novak <claire@asteria.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Asteria Procurement <procurement@asteria.health>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@asteria.health>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from Friday's intro — procurement & security checklist

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. That aligns with procurement's expectations. Quick answers from our side: 

- Preferred payment for pilot: PO with a 30-day payment term if possible. Card is acceptable for smaller pilot spend but procurement prefers PO for vendor onboarding.
- Marketplace: we are evaluating GCP Marketplace for later stages, but procurement will still need the same security artifacts if billed through marketplace.
- Security gating: procurement requires SOC 2 Type II (or a letter from an auditor) and a signed DPA. I attached our standard vendor security questionnaire — can your team populate the marked tabs?

Target timeline: procurement aiming for vendor onboarding by end of November if artifacts are provided this week.

Thanks,
Claire Novak
Head of Platform Partnerships, Asteria Health
claire@asteria.health

Attachment: Asteria_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@asteria.health>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from Friday's intro — procurement & security checklist

Claire / team — I pulled the questionnaire and started filling in the control rows. Key notes: 
- SOC 2: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II 2025 coverage; I attached the executive summary. We can provide the full report under NDA or via secure link.
- DPA: our standard Redwood_DPA_Template.pdf covers data handling specifics. For additional clauses, we can negotiate redlines but 80% of customers accept the template as-is.
- Questionnaire items flagged: encryption key management (we support KMS/HSM integrations), data retention policy (configurable per-customer), and incident response SLA (we have 24/7 incident paging + formal RCA cadence).

Action items: 
- I'll upload the completed questionnaire (tab "Redwood responses") to your drive link and send a DocuSign-ready DPA to procurement for signature.
- If procurement insists on PO only, we can attach a commercial addendum showing net-30 terms. Marissa, can you draft that?

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template.pdf

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: next steps — PO paperwork, DPA, and marketplace note (internal)

Internal note — keeping this short so we can move procurement along: 

1) Marissa: please put together a one-page commercial options memo (PO net-30, card, GCP marketplace) with pricing footnotes for the pilot. Procurement prefers PO — include a sample PO flow and the onboarding timeline if they choose marketplace vs direct billing. Target: EOD 17 Nov.
2) Ben: finalize the questionnaire responses and upload the completed sheet to the Drive link Claire provided. Also prepare the DocuSign DPA envelope and loop Marcus on the sign-flow.
3) Marcus: I'll confirm with Claire that we can deliver the full SOC 2 report via secure link (require NDA or vendor portal access) and propose next internal review call on 11/19 if procurement wants to sign off.

Also note: if procurement pushes for marketplace billing, there may be a 2-3 week delay depending on marketplace onboarding — call that out in the memo.

Let me know if anything blocks you. We want to keep this to the end-of-month onboarding target.

Marcus
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0126
